task.title: Backup Configuration Settings
task.shortdesc: Create and store a backup of the configuration. Use the backup to restore approved network settings after a configuration error, factory reset, or hardware replacement.

prereq.p: Before you create a configuration backup, make sure that:

ul.li: A computer is connected to the .
You have the credentials for the .
The current network configuration operates correctly.
The computer has sufficient storage space for the backup file.
You have access to a secure location for the backup file.

prereq.note: Use a wired connection when possible. Do not disconnect the router or computer while the backup file is created.

context.p: A configuration backup contains the saved settings for the . These settings can include the Wi-Fi configuration, guest network settings, DHCP settings, access-control rules, and other network settings.
Create a backup after the initial setup and after an important configuration change.
context.note: A configuration backup does not back up files from computers, smartphones, storage devices, or other client devices.
Record the product model, hardware version, firmware version, and configuration state for each backup. Confirm compatibility before you restore a backup to different hardware or firmware.
A configuration backup can contain sensitive network information. Store the backup file in a secure location.

step.cmd: Verify that the network operates correctly.

substep.cmd: Confirm that an authorized client device can connect to .
Confirm that the client device can access Internet services.
Confirm that the required guest, IoT, access-point, and mesh connections operate correctly.

info.note: Do not create an approved baseline backup from a configuration that has known errors.

step.stepresult: The current configuration is suitable for backup.

step.cmd: Open a supported web browser on the connected computer.

step.stepresult: The sign-in page for the opens.

substep.cmd: Enter in the user name field.

info.p: The backup settings can appear under Administration, System, Maintenance, or the .
info.note: Menu and control names can differ by .

step.cmd: Record the current product and software information.

info.note: Do not record Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, or other confidential credentials.

step.cmd: Select the option to create or export a configuration backup.

info.p: The control can appear as Back Up, Export Configuration, or Save Configuration.

step.cmd: Configure backup-file protection if this option is available.

info.p: Use encryption or a strong backup password if the provides this function.
Store the backup password separately from the backup file.
info.note: If you lose the backup password, you might not be able to restore the configuration.

step.cmd: Save the backup file to the computer.

info.p: Select a secure local folder. Do not save the file in a public or shared download folder.
info.note: Do not change the file extension or edit the contents of the backup file.

step.stepresult: The configuration backup file is saved to the computer.

step.cmd: Give the backup file an identifiable name.

info.p: Include the product model, firmware version, backup date, and configuration state in the file name.
info.note: Do not include a password, username, public IP address, or other sensitive information in the file name.
Use only characters permitted by the operating system and the backup process.

step.cmd: Verify that the backup file was created.

substep.cmd: Open the folder that contains the backup file.
Confirm that the backup file has a file name and a file size greater than zero.
Confirm that the backup date and product information are correct.

info.note: Do not open or edit the backup file with a text editor, archive tool, or other application.

step.stepresult: The backup file is present and identifiable.

step.cmd: Record a checksum for the backup file if your maintenance process requires integrity verification.

info.p: Store the checksum in the maintenance record. Use the checksum to identify an unintended change to the backup file.
info.note: A checksum identifies file changes. A checksum does not encrypt or protect the contents of the file.

step.cmd: Copy the backup file to a secure storage location.

info.p: Use an encrypted storage device, an access-controlled network location, or another approved storage location.
info.note: Do not store the only backup copy on the or on a client device that can be easily lost or damaged.

step.cmd: Create an additional protected copy of the backup.

info.p: Store the additional copy in a separate approved location. Use access controls and encryption as required by the applicable security policy.
info.note: A separate copy protects the configuration from device failure, accidental deletion, or damage to the primary storage location.

ul.li: The person or role that created the backup
The configuration changes included in the backup

info.note: Do not include passwords, encryption keys, backup passwords, access tokens, or other confidential credentials in the backup record.

info.p: Close the browser if you used a shared computer.

result.p: A backup of the configuration is stored in a secure location. The backup record identifies the product and configuration associated with the file.

ul.li: A Wi-Fi or security configuration change
A DHCP or IP address configuration change
A new access point or mesh-node configuration
A successful recovery from a configuration problem

postreq.p: Keep only the backup versions required by the applicable maintenance and retention policy.
postreq.note: Securely delete a backup that is obsolete or no longer authorized for use.
